cannot use cards until after combat. does this mean only from that
point on, or does it also exclude the use of cards already in play?

also, what if flesh of marble was played before thoughts betrayed.
would thoughts betrayed cancel the effect of that card?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
tirn...@mindspring.com (I/O) writes:
>o.k., here's the question. thoughts betrayed - opposing minions
>cannot use cards until after combat. does this mean only from that
>point on, or does it also exclude the use of cards already in play?
>i.e. could i still use my equipment or cards such as dog pack.

It only prevents cards from being played - the opposing minion could
still make full use of equipment/retainers/Elysiums, etc.

>also, what if flesh of marble was played before thoughts betrayed.
>would thoughts betrayed cancel the effect of that card?

Flesh of Marble cannot be played before TB. TB is played "as combat
is entered", flesh is played after that point (within combat).

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
I/O (tirn...@mindspring.com) wrote:

: o.k., here's the question. thoughts betrayed - opposing minions

: cannot use cards until after combat. does this mean only from that
: point on, or does it also exclude the use of cards already in play?
: i.e. could i still use my equipment or cards such as dog pack.

It was ruled that cards already in play could be used. You simply may
not play cards from your hand after a superior TB.

: also, what if flesh of marble was played before thoughts betrayed.

: would thoughts betrayed cancel the effect of that card?

It couldn't be. TB is played at the last moment before combat begins
(or the first moment after combat is entered -- take your pick), and thus
is played AFTER all modifiers, but BEFORE all combat cards. FoM would HAVE
to be played AFTER a TB, sorry to say.

-spongy

Messages.Author: staffan.bengtsson
Messages.Body:
>o.k., here's the question. thoughts betrayed - opposing minions
>cannot use cards until after combat. does this mean only from that
>point on, or does it also exclude the use of cards already in play?
>i.e. could i still use my equipment or cards such as dog pack.

The card have a errata that says that cards may not be played OUT
during combat. That means that you could still use your equipment/retainers as
normal.

>also, what if flesh of marble was played before thoughts betrayed.
>would thoughts betrayed cancel the effect of that card?

Since Thoughts Betrayed is a combat card it must be played during combat
instead of "before combat begins".
"Before combat begins" is still effective anyway becouse Thoughts betrayed
goes before all other COMBAT cards including flesh of Marble.

You could not cancel the acting minions attempt to use stealth modifiers or the
blocking minon to use obedience by the way.

Messages.Author: Stuart J. Pieloch
Messages.Body:
joh...@hp.com hath spake thusly:

>The only other question is wheather can you play a disguised or
>concealed weapon before a thoughts betrayed.

You may not play any combat cards while under the superior effects of
a Thoughts Betrayed. You may use any card currently on the table, but
no combat card may come out of your hand onto the soon to be hosed
vamp.

Stu

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <32D37F...@hp.com>,

joh...@hp.com wrote:
>
> The only other question is wheather can you play a disguised or
> concealed weapon before a thoughts betrayed.

No. Both Concealed Weapon and Disguised Weapon are combat
cards, so are only playable from within combat.

TB beats both because it is a combat cards that has the explicit
card text making played "as combat is entered". No other combat
card can be played before TB.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
2 blood
Dominate
Combat
Only usable before combat begins. Opposing minion takes an additional 1
damage in the first round of combat during strike resolution.
(S) Only usable before combat begins. Opposing minion cannot use any
cards until after combat.
Dave Roach and Pete Burges
Common

Text of Disguised Weapon:

Disguised Weapon
Obfuscate
Combat
Only usable before range is chosen. Equip this vampire with a weapon
card from your hand (and pay cost to equip).
(M) As above, but only usable when choosing a strike.
Anson Maddocks
Common

Before combat begins means just after you've both declared that you're
not upping stealth and intercept any more and combat has just begun

Before range is chosen means before you have chosen range by declaring
maneuvers

I don't see any reason why you couldn't play a Disguised Weapon before

the Thoughts Betrayed since they both happen during a combat and playing
a Disguised Weapon at the start of the round *is* before range is
chosen.

It's the same sort of thing with Blood to Water (from AH). You play
that before Strike Resolution:

Blood to Water
2 blood
Thaumaturgy
Combat
Use before strike resolution. If the opposing minion is a vampire, he or
she burns 3 blood before strike resolution; otherwise, he or she is
burned.
Not usable during the first round of combat.
(S) As above, but if the opposing minion is a vampire, he or she burns 5
blood.
Liz Danforth
Common 2

However, it doesn't state directly before the strike is resolved, so you
could play it at the start of the round, during the range or even after
you've both declared strikes but before you've resolved them.

So, the simple answer to your question is:

Yes, you can Disguised Weapon before Thoughts Betrayed (well, I think so
anyway)

--
James Coupe.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
James Coupe <Jus...@bgrace.demon.co.uk> writes:
>Before combat begins means just after you've both declared that you're
>not upping stealth and intercept any more and combat has just begun

>Before range is chosen means before you have chosen range by declaring
>maneuvers

Yes to both. "Before combat begins" has been ruled to mean "as combat
is entered".

>I don't see any reason why you couldn't play a Disguised Weapon before

>the Thoughts Betrayed since they both happen during a combat and playing
>a Disguised Weapon at the start of the round *is* before range is
>chosen.

The reason is that you can't play combat cards before combat, and
TB is played as the combat is enetred - before any other combat
card can be played. (TB is granted special timing by its "before
combat" wording.)

>It's the same sort of thing with Blood to Water (from AH). You play
>that before Strike Resolution:

>However, it doesn't state directly before the strike is resolved, so you

>could play it at the start of the round, during the range or even after
>you've both declared strikes but before you've resolved them.

Yes by card text, but this has been ruled to be playable only in the
"before resolution" phase - that is, the space between declare strikes
and resolve strikes. (and only if the round is at close range.)
